Why does the Ticket Booth pick the discount with one if / elif / else chain?
options: Because elif runs faster than if
Because a customer is in exactly one age group, so exactly one discount must be picked
Because Python allows only one if in a program

questions.text: In the chain below, why doesn't `elif age <= 12:` also check that age is at least 6?
options: It should, or a 4-year-old gets 5 EUR off
Because elif checks every number from 6 to 12 by itself
Because Python only reaches the elif when age < 6 was false
Because 6 is the default value of age

questions.text: What goes wrong if `elif age <= 64:` comes right after `if age < 6:`, before `elif age <= 12:`?
options: Nothing, the order of the elifs doesn't matter
Only customers over 64 get the wrong discount
A child of 8 gets no discount: the first true condition wins and the rest are skipped

questions.text: What does Python do first in `total = price - discount`?
options: It works out price - discount, then stores the result in total
It stores price in total, then subtracts discount from price
It checks whether total equals price - discount
It stores the text price - discount in total

questions.text: What does `total = total + 2` do?
options: It checks whether total is 2 more than before
It adds 2 to total and stores the new value back in total
It stops with an error: total can't be on both sides
It makes a second variable called total

questions.text: Why is the 3D fee checked with its own if after the age chain, not with one more elif inside it?
options: Because elif can't check True or False
Because the fee comes on top of any discount, and an elif would be skipped once an age branch runs
Because an if after a chain always runs
